data.description:
Chain link 4, "issues an invoice on that client, on the freelancer's own account" — server side. Create-or-reuse the Stripe customer (cus_) on the connected account, create invoice items and the invoice (collection_method=send_invoice, days_until_due), finalize it, send it, and persist the mirror record (status, hosted_invoice_url, invoice_pdf).

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 rows C-26 (Stripe customer mirror), C-27 (invoice draft) and C-28 (finalize and send). All IN under Rule 1.

DECISION CONTEXT. Every call carries Stripe-Account: acct_... and goes through the custody-guard wrapper. This is the exact sequence the D1 spike validated against stripe-mock (docs/strategy/spikes/spike-D1-freelancer-invoicing.md section 1): /v1/customers then /v1/invoiceitems then /v1/invoices then /finalize then /send, all scoped to the connected account — so the charge lands on the freelancer's account and never on ours.

DO NOT PASS application_fee_amount. The board has not ruled on the app-fee reading of constraint 7 and subscription-only is the operative default (docs/strategy/08-board-decision.md section 3.2). The spike measured that reversing this is one parameter on this one call; that option is preserved by the wrapper's existence, not by writing the path.

Sending is Stripe's job: POST /v1/invoices/:id/send makes STRIPE email the client, under the connected account's branding, on Stripe's sender infrastructure. That is why our own invoice email (row C-31) and our own invoice PDF (row C-30) are OUT under Rule 2 — and it is how the client learns about the invoice in a v1 that can send no email of its own. Finalize is gated on the connected account's readiness flag maintained by the Connect task: read the flag, do not re-derive it.

VERIFICATION: request shapes validated against stripe-mock; sequencing, the readiness gate, and mirror persistence unit-tested against fixture responses. Size note (milestone plan section 8.2 tripwire): projected around 550 lines including tests, just under the 600-line split threshold — kept as one task because it is one reviewable claim ("a draft invoice can be created, finalized and sent on the freelancer's own account"). NAMED RESIDUAL: real state transitions and the client-facing email are not observable against stripe-mock, which is stateless; the test-mode acceptance run confirms them.

NOT IN THIS TASK: any application-fee or take-rate parameter, ever (row C-42); webhook handling or status sync; the invoice screens; reminders or manual re-sends (rows C-39 and C-40, OUT — Rule 1, and Stripe's own reminder cadences ride on the connected account at zero cost to us, configured by the freelancer in their own Stripe Dashboard); multi-currency or VAT fields (row C-32).
data.title: D1 v1: invoice lifecycle (server) — customer mirror, draft, finalize, send

data.note: Stripe-touching: every call goes through the custody guard
invoice mirror and client records; readiness flag is read from here

data.body:
Pulled as the top D1 pull: it is the only remaining high on the spine, both its dependencies (AS-38 custody client, AS-39 persistence) are done, and AS-44's webhook receiver sits directly behind it. Marcus implements — he built AS-38, AS-39 and AS-41, which is the entire surface this task composes. Owen plans as tech lead; Priya or Ruben reviews (implementer != reviewer, and Priya's AS-41 review already covers the readiness contract this task reads).

Still WIP=1: the AS-60 lanes carve-out is merged as a written result but NOT shipped, its verdict is qualified, and the board's veto window on it is open (#board msg 448). This task runs under current rules.

Plan written (tech lead: cto-owen). THREE OPERATIONS, four routes: POST /invoices and POST /invoices/{id} are LOCAL draft create/update (zero Stripe calls); POST /invoices/{id}/finalize runs the push pipeline through finalize; POST /invoices/{id}/send runs the same pipeline through send (it does not stop early) — so the wireframe's single 'Finalize & send' control is one POST and AS-49 can still drive the steps separately. Five connected-scope Stripe calls, all already on AS-38's allowlist: NO allowlist row is added and custody.js is not edited.

FINALIZE GATE: read repos.connectedAccounts.getByFreelancer(F).ready — AS-39's single derivation, restated nowhere. Refusal is 403 AccountNotReadyError with step not-connected|not-ready, before any Stripe call. Distinguishable from InvalidStateError/AmountMismatchError (409) by status, class and step; 403 is used by nothing else.

LAZY CUSTOMER: AS-41's three layers reused, not reinvented — row check, stable idempotency key cus-create-<clientId>, convergence on the stored cus_ (setStripeCustomerId is a no-op for the same id, so the common double-submit simply agrees). Stripe first, row after.

DECLARED FILE SCOPE (§2): allowed prefix set = [apps/invoicing/], nothing else. New: lib/invoices/mapping.js, lib/invoices/lifecycle.js, routes/invoices.js, test/invoices.test.js. Modified: app.js, test/harness.test.js, test/dependency-policy.test.js, README.md.

AS-44 BOUNDARY: this task writes draft and open only; AS-44 writes paid/void/uncollectible/lastPaymentFailedAt. Both go through the SAME applyStripeSnapshot rank machine — one rule, two callers. AS-44 inherits lib/invoices/mapping.js, whose ten-key output deliberately excludes sentAt and lastPaymentFailedAt so a later full snapshot cannot erase them (R23 tests exactly that interaction).

Two design decisions worth the board-legible record: (1) the invoice is created BEFORE its items and each item names invoice=in_ explicitly, inverting the spike diagram's order — pending invoice items attach to the CUSTOMER, so a failed run would sweep them onto the next invoice for the same client; (2) a reconciliation guard refuses the send if Stripe's amount_due or currency disagrees with ours after finalize. 20 ACs, 7 falsification recipes, ~1,220 lines / 8 files projected (tripwire justification + pre-agreed split line in §8).

Measured while planning, against stripe-mock v0.203.0 at 2026-08-26.dahlia: POST /v1/invoiceitems REJECTS unit_amount (400) at this API version — the naive quantity+unit_amount shape does not exist and would have failed at the first contract run. Recorded in the plan preamble with four other measurements.

Also corrected AS-41's plan §7 in place (F1/F2 predicted sets and F2's rationale, per Priya's review comment; F6/F7 added as standing recipes), marked as post-review corrections rather than silently rewritten.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-43 on feat/AS-43-invoice-lifecycle, per the plan: lazy customer creation, draft local-only, the five connected-account calls with per-object idempotency keys, the 403 finalize gate reading AS-39's single ready derivation, and the shared mapper AS-44 inherits. Falsification recipes with backups outside apps/invoicing/; isolated compose project only.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — 3 commits on feat/AS-43-invoice-lifecycle, worktree clean.

FILES (git diff --shortstat master...): 8 files, 1,831 insertions, 13 deletions.
  new      lib/invoices/mapping.js            109
  new      lib/invoices/lifecycle.js          321
  new      routes/invoices.js                 250
  new      test/invoices.test.js            1,021  (cap is 1,200)
  mod      app.js                              +8/-2
  mod      test/dependency-policy.test.js     +26/-5
  mod      test/harness.test.js                +5/-2
  mod      README.md                         +104/-4
Commits: 7a35377 source+dependency-policy literals | e939a4f tests+harness literal | 42efa8a README.
Each commit carries the literals its own change moved, and each was verified green in isolation
(the source commit was run with invoices.test.js off disk and harness still at 11: 215 tests, 200
pass, 0 fail).

SUITES
  test (offline, network_mode: none) — exit 0, 241 tests, 223 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped.
  contract (stripe-mock)             — exit 0, 241 tests, 241 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.
  V1 instrument check both ways: ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 -> exit 1; plain -> exit 0.
  The 18 skips, enumerated: 12 from stripe-mock.test.js (reachable/not-Stripe, strict-version,
  the 5 connected shapes, GET /v1/invoices/{id}, the 3 platform shapes, unknown-parameter,
  idempotency/request-id echo, forbidden-shape-accepted-raw), 3 from connect.test.js (M1-M3),
  3 from invoices.test.js (M1-M3). All 18 report as SKIPPED, never as passed.

PLAN PREAMBLE RE-MEASURED before writing code (throwaway loopback stripe-mock v0.203.0,
Stripe-Version 2026-08-26.dahlia). All five findings reproduce exactly: unit_amount on
/v1/invoiceitems is a 400 "additional properties are not allowed"; invoice=in_ accepted;
pending_invoice_items_behavior=exclude accepted; the invoice fixture is the constant
{status draft, amount_due 1000, amount_paid 0, both URLs null, due_date 1234567890,
status_transitions all null}, identical from create/finalize/send; no sent_at on the object.
MOCK_FIXTURE_AMOUNT_DUE = 1000 confirmed and M1/M3 are built on it.

FALSIFICATION RECIPES (each one indivisible: backup outside apps/invoicing/, mutate,
assert-applied, run in container, restore under trap, prove, rebuild, re-run green).

F1  delete both gate throws | applied: throws 2->0, marker 2
    predicted EXACT {R7,R8} — observed {R7,R8}. MATCH.
F2  drop account: from the finalize call only | applied: `account:` 5->4, marker 1
    predicted LOWER BOUND {R6,R11,R12,R13,R14,R15,R18,R22} — observed
    {R6,R9,R10,R11,R12,R13,R15,R22}. Same size, membership differs both ways:
    + R9 and R10 fail because their FIRST finalize is a fresh draft that does reach step 4
      (the plan's "R9/R10/R16 skip step 4" is true only of their second action);
    - R14 stays green: it sends from an already-OPEN invoice, so steps 3-4 are skipped and
      it never touches the mutated call;
    - R18 stays green: with no key, requireKey fires at the FIRST call (create-customer,
      still custody-legal), so the run never reaches the mutated finalize. The guard does
      precede requireKey, but only for the same call.
F3  duplicate the push (same idempotency key) | applied: /v1/invoiceitems sites 1->2, marker 1
    predicted LOWER BOUND {R6,R11,R12,R15,R22} offline, M-cases unaffected — observed offline
    {R6,R9,R15,R22}; contract run: same 4, M1-M3 GREEN.
    NARROWER by {R11,R12}, wider by {R9}. Cause, and it is deviation 3 below: the fixture
    models Stripe's idempotency window, so a duplicate under the SAME key is absorbed exactly
    as Stripe would absorb it — the totals do not diverge and the reconciliation guard
    correctly does not fire; the mutation is caught by the exact call-count assertions instead.
    The plan's prediction assumed a pure accumulator, which is a Stripe that does not exist and
    which cannot pass R11 at all. Tests were NOT narrowed to match. The M-case asymmetry the
    plan predicted is confirmed: the mock's amount_due is a constant, so it is structurally
    incapable of catching a duplicated line item; only the computing fixture can.
F3b ADDED, because F3 as written no longer exercises the guard: duplicate the push with the
    duplicate's idempotency key REMOVED — the lapsed-window case the guard actually defends.
    applied: sites 1->2 and the duplicate verified verbatim to carry no idempotencyKey.
    Observed {R6,R9,R10,R11,R15,R22} and the guard fires: R10's first finalize is 409 != 303.
    The reconciliation guard is therefore demonstrated failing, not merely seen passing.
F4  add sentAt: null to the mapper | applied: 'sentAt:' 0->1 (any-sentAt 2->3, the other two are
    comments), marker 1. predicted EXACT {R1,R23} with R14/R15 green — observed exactly that.
    MATCH, and R14/R15 staying green confirms the spread order {...mapper, sentAt: now()}.
F5  delete the customer-reuse skip | applied: predicate 2->1 (the survivor is the header
    diagram line), marker 1. predicted EXACT {R9} plus {R10,R16}, flagged LOWER BOUND if more
    zero-calls-on-repeat cases exist — observed {R9,R10,R11,R14,R16}. WIDER by {R11,R14},
    which are exactly such cases (R11 pins zero second /v1/customers on the retry; R14 pins the
    exact one-call list). Lower bound observed wider = pass.
F6  scratch copy of the app + tokens + .dockerignore under TMPDIR, invoices.test.js renamed
    there ONLY; task worktree untouched throughout (0 uncommitted entries before and after).
    predicted EXACT harness V2 with a specific message — observed harness V2 only, message
    verbatim: "expected exactly 12 test files, found 11: assets…, config…, connect…, db…,
    dependency-policy…, deploy-shape…, harness…, health…, repositories…, stripe-client…,
    stripe-mock…". MATCH. Scratch copy and its image removed.
F7  revert the money-words list to its pre-AS-43 four entries | applied: row 7->4
    predicted EXACT the concept test only — observed exactly that, message naming the three
    new files as found-but-not-allowed. MATCH.
F7b ADDED (the mirror direction): list money-word-FREE app.js in the money row | applied:
    marker 1, money row only. Observed the concept test only, failing on the used-exemption
    direction — which independently re-proves that app.js gained no money word.

PROCEDURAL FINDING on the recipes themselves: the plan's restore proof, "prove the tree with
git diff --exit-code", is VACUOUS for a file git has never seen — git diff does not inspect
untracked files, so for F1-F3 (run before the first commit) it could only ever have reported the
other, legitimate work-in-progress. Those three were proven restored by byte-comparison against
the backup plus a marker grep; I then committed and re-ran F4-F7 against a clean tracked tree,
where git diff --exit-code is a real check and did report TREE CLEAN each time. Recommend the
next plan say: prove with diff-against-backup, and with git only once the file is committed.

TEST LITERALS THAT MOVED — exactly the four in plan 5.4, and nothing else:
  1. harness EXPECTED_TEST_FILES gains 'invoices.test.js' at sorted position 9; cardinality
     11 -> 12 in both the number and the message (and the "eleven files" prose in the V2 comment).
  2. dependency-policy source list 29 -> 32: lib/invoices/lifecycle.js, lib/invoices/mapping.js
     (between lib/health.js and lib/stripe/client.js) and routes/invoices.js (between
     routes/health.js and routes/pages.js).
  3. dependency-policy money-words RAW row 4 -> 7 entries. All three new files genuinely carry a
     money word (measured raw hits: lifecycle 15, mapping 6, routes 8), so all three were listed
     and none was listed hopefully. app.js gained none — verified by grep AND by F7b.
  4. The concept test's name gains AS-43. The 'platform Stripe call' row's allowed list is
     UNCHANGED, as claimed: this diff adds no platform-scoped call (grep: 0 in all three files).
MUST-NOT-MOVE set, confirmed unmoved: LOCK_ENTRIES 70, DIRECT_DEPENDENCIES [ejs, express],
SANCTIONED.length 3, manifests 3, config SCHEMA rows 10, and deploy-shape / health / db /
repositories / connect / stripe-client / stripe-mock / assets untouched (they are not in the
diff at all — git diff --stat lists 8 files).
TRAPS in 5.4 item 5, all clear in the new files: STRIPE_[A-Z_]+ 0, raw SQL 0, fetch 0,
transport.js import 0, stripe package import 0, quoted "/webhook" 0, application_fee 0,
platform: true 0, test file 1,021 lines (< 1,200).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. 1-16 met. AC 5 checked by grep as specified: the ONE derivation occurs
exactly once app-wide (connected-accounts.js:48) and none of the four readiness identifiers
appears anywhere in this diff (0 in all 8 files — my first draft of a lifecycle.js COMMENT
named them, which is itself an AC 5 violation, and it was reworded). AC 14: no 'paid'/'void'/
'uncollectible' literal is written by this task's source. AC 17: verified file by file —
custody.js (9 allowlist rows, unchanged), client.js, transport.js, lib/db/** (0 files),
config.js, routes/connect.js, lib/connect/*, server.js, test/helpers/server.js, compose.yaml,
Dockerfile, package.json, package-lock.json all unchanged. AC 18 and 19 as above. AC 20 above.

DEVIATIONS, numbered.
1. quantity is NOT sent on /v1/invoiceitems. Plan 3.5's prose bullet says "plus quantity for
   display", but 3.5's own Params column and 5.3's R6 assertion list both enumerate the item
   body without it, and AC 3 pins "exactly 3.5's table". I measured that stripe-mock accepts
   amount+quantity together (200, echoing quantity: 2) — but the mock validates parameter NAMES,
   not mutual exclusivity, so it cannot adjudicate the real API's documented "only one of
   amount, quantity" rule, and this is a money-adjacent call. Went with the table and R6; the
   line's structure is carried by description. One parameter on one call if the CTO wants
   display quantity — same shape as Q2, and AS-50 is where it becomes observable.
2. No comment was added to routes/connect.js. Plan 3.1 and 3.2 ask for a one-line comment "in
   each" file (the shared seam; the ValidationError 400-vs-502 divergence), but section 2 lists
   routes/connect.js under "Not modified, and that is a claim to check" and AC 17 requires zero
   changes to it. AC 17 wins; both comments live in routes/invoices.js and name connect.js.
3. The fixture transport models Stripe's idempotency window (~6 lines): a replayed key returns
   the same reply and contributes nothing further to the running total; replies produced by an
   intercept are never cached, so a failed call stays retryable. Plan 5.3 specs a pure
   accumulator, under which R11's retry re-pushes, the total doubles, the guard refuses with 409
   and R11 cannot pass — making AC 11 untestable. This models plan 3.8's own stated mechanism.
   Consequence for F3 recorded above; F3b added rather than weakening the fixture.
4. Two cases widened (additions, not substitutions): R3 also asserts an oversized body is 413
   through the router-scoped parser, and R5 also asserts a past-the-limit index is 400.

LIBRARY FACT that contradicts the plan's reasoning and is now recorded in the test: body-parser
2.x sets qs's arrayLimit to Math.max(100, <this request's parameter count>) — a threshold that
MOVES WITH THE REQUEST, not the fixed 20 the plan assumed. So R5's 25 items arrive as a dense
ARRAY, not the numeric-keyed object plan 3.3 says the case exists to cover, and a sparse set
below the limit is silently COMPACTED (indexes 0 and 30 arrive as a 2-element array). The object
branch is reachable only above index ~100, which with MAX_LINE_ITEMS = 50 always means a
refusal — so the normaliser's object branch is defensive-only under today's express. Both
branches were kept (a limit derived from request size is a stronger reason not to depend on it),
and R5 now covers both, but the plan's stated rationale for R5 is stale. This cost one red run
and is exactly the "library default this plan refuses to depend on" it warned about.

SIZE vs THE SPLIT LINE: 1,831 insertions, so the diff DID cross plan 8's ~1,400 pre-agreed split
line. I did not split — reporting it for the CTO's call, per instruction. Note if you do: the
named split (M1-M3 + R11 + R5 into a follow-up) would remove currently-passing coverage from
this branch, including the only two cases that exercise resumption and the parser at scale.

LEFT UNDONE / RESIDUAL, restated not resolved (AC 16): stripe-mock is stateless, so draft ->
open -> paid, the client-facing email, Stripe's actual deduplication of our five idempotency
keys, and whether a real amount_due equals our computed total on a live account are all
unobservable here. They belong to AS-50's acceptance run, gated on AS-51. No Stripe account
exists, none was opened, no board ask filed. No new dependency, no allowlist row, no migration,
no compose/Dockerfile/config change.

HOUSEKEEPING: isolated compose project asc-invoicing-as43 torn down profile-aware (the
stripe-mock container a plain `down` leaves behind was removed); every image I built removed,
including the 30 dangling intermediates from my rebuild cycles; stripe/stripe-mock:v0.203.0 left
pulled; asc-invoicing-web-1 and asc-chat-server-1 untouched and healthy throughout. Unrelated
observation for the CTO, NOT touched: 238 dangling docker images remain on this host dating back
to 2026-07-29 — a repo-wide housekeeping backlog, and a candidate for its own small task.

REVIEWER, START HERE: (1) lifecycle.js reconcile() and the order in finalizeInvoice — snapshot
written before the refusal is the one deliberately surprising choice; (2) deviation 1, the
absent quantity, which is the one place I chose the plan's table over its prose on a
money-adjacent call; (3) deviation 3 plus F3/F3b together — whether you agree the fixture should
model idempotency and that F3b is the honest falsification of the guard; (4) the F2 and F5
divergences, both reasoned from the call pipeline above.

Split-line call (plan §8): measured 1,844 lines changed across 8 files vs the ~1,400 pre-agreed line. NOT splitting. The file count is exactly the planned 8 — no scope crept in; the overrun is test density, and the implementer notes a split would remove the only two cases exercising resumption and the parser at scale, i.e. it would delete coverage rather than defer it. Same call and same reasoning as AS-39 (3,161 lines, reviewed whole, passed in one cycle). The plan's second trigger stands as the backstop: if review reaches cycle 2 on scope grounds, §8's split line applies as written.

Also recording, because it is the more valuable finding of the two: the plan's restore proof (git diff --exit-code) is VACUOUS for a file git has never seen. Recipes run before the first commit can only ever report unrelated work-in-progress, so an unrestored mutation in a new file would pass that check silently. The implementer caught it mid-stage, proved F1-F3 restored by byte-comparison against the out-of-tree backup plus a marker grep, then committed and re-ran F4-F7 against a tracked tree where the check is real. This is a defect in the house falsification recipe itself, not in this task: the recipe template should require either a tracked tree or an explicit byte-comparison. Carrying it to the metawork layer rather than fixing it inside a task.
